title: Strictly semistable modifications are cofinal over a strict model
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $Y$ be a strictly semistable $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $q:W\to Y$ be a modification. There is a strictly semistable $T$-curve $Z$ and an $\eta$-modification $Z\to Y$ factoring as $Z\to W\to Y$, with $Z\to W$ itself an $\eta$-modification. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A $T$-curve is strictly semistable if, locally on it and on $T$, it admits an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$, where $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open of $T$ and $a\in A$; polynomial rings use [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. A modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens; an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense if $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. An $\eta$-modification is also an isomorphism on the whole generic fibre.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-strict-semistable-model-normal], $Y$ is normal and reduced. Take the empty marking and apply [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] to $Y$: it has finitely many irreducible components. The given $W$ is reduced as well: on the schematically dense isomorphism opens it is isomorphic to an open of reduced $Y$, and the injection $\mathcal O_W\hookrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_U$ kills every nilpotent local section. The same horizontal-model statement therefore applies to $W\to Y$ and shows that $W$ is a $T$-curve and $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism. This does not assume that the original modification was already declared an $\eta$-modification.

source.place: Section 4.2, introductory paragraph; Proposition 4.3.1, normality input

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-fibre-valuation-domination] to $q:W\to Y$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1. Obtain a finite set $F=\{\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_n\}$, each with a specified centre morphism to $Y$, residual transcendence degree one, and closed centre on $Y$. To dominate $W$ it suffices to construct a normal modification of $Y$ on which all these centres are generic points of their $T$-fibres. This criterion is applied to the fixed target $Y$, throughout.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, first paragraph, finite-set reduction using Proposition 4.2.3

proof.text: Composites in the construction below are $\eta$-modifications. Indeed, $\eta$ is open in $T$: if $V=K$ this is immediate; otherwise choose a nonzero $c$ in the least nonzero prime ideal of $V$, so that $D(c)=\{\eta\}$. On any flat affine $T$-chart its ring injects into its localization over $K$, so the generic fibre is schematically dense. Thus for maps of $T$-curves which are proper and isomorphisms on the generic fibre, the whole generic fibres are schematically dense isomorphism opens. A composite of two such maps is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a) and is still a generic-fibre isomorphism, hence is again an $\eta$-modification.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, first paragraph, iteration; only modification cofinality is required, so no theorem on composing blow-ups is needed

proof.text:
Set $Y_0=Y$. Inductively construct strictly semistable $T$-curves $Y_j$ and $\eta$-modifications $p_j:Y_j	o Y$ such that $
u_1,\ldots,
u_j$ have generic fibre centres on $Y_j$. The identity gives the base $j=0$. Every $Y_j$ is normal by [lem-trf-strict-semistable-model-normal], and its generic fibre is smooth because $p_{j,\eta}$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-trf-finite-fibre-valuation-domination], $
u_{j+1}$ has a unique lifted centre on $Y_j$; it is either a generic point of its $T$-fibre or is closed on $Y_j$. If already generic, put $Y_{j+1}=Y_j$. Otherwise apply [lem-trf-single-valuation-semistable-extraction] to this lifted valuation on $Y_j$. Its valuation ring, function field and residual transcendence degree have not changed, and the closed-centre hypothesis was just checked. It gives a strictly semistable $\eta$-modification $Y_{j+1}	o Y_j$ making this centre generic. Compose with $p_j$ using Step 3.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, first paragraph, iterative extraction of a finite set using the single-valuation claim proved on pp. 28--29

proof.text: The induction does not lose any of the first $j$ centres: since $Y_j$ is normal, the last assertion of [lem-trf-finite-fibre-valuation-domination] says that the modification $Y_{j+1}\to Y_j$ is an isomorphism near their fibre generic centres. They therefore remain generic fibre centres on $Y_{j+1}$. This proves the inductive invariant. After $n$ steps set $Z=Y_n$ and $p=p_n$; all of $F$ is extracted. If $F$ is empty this construction gives $Z=Y$ without any extraction.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, finite iteration; persistence uses Lemma 4.2.1(i)

proof.text: Normality of $Z$ follows again from [lem-trf-strict-semistable-model-normal]. Apply [lem-trf-finite-fibre-valuation-domination] to $p:Z\to Y$ and the original $q:W\to Y$. It supplies a modification $h:Z\to W$ with $qh=p$. On the generic fibre, $h_\eta=q_\eta^{-1}p_\eta$ is an isomorphism, since both $q_\eta$ and $p_\eta$ are. Thus $h$ is an $\eta$-modification. The construction already gives strictly semistable $Z$ and an $\eta$-modification $p$ to $Y$, with the required factorization.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, conclusion of first paragraph by Proposition 4.2.3

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-308860345 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all three new nodes and the cited statements (horizontal-curve-models, proper-fp-permanence), plus the parent's use of the item and unit sk-i-curve-zero. The item statement is byte-identical to the side DAG's version, so it is not weakened. Steps 1-6 are correct: W is shown reduced via the injection into j_*O_U; eta is open because the primes form a finite chain (D(c)={eta}); flatness makes the generic fibre schematically dense; the induction states its invariant and keeps earlier centres via the last clause of the domination node; h_eta=q_eta^-1 p_eta. I checked the three new statements myself and found no false clause. Normality: A[t] and A[u,v]/(uv-a) with a nonzero are normal, normality ascends along etale maps, and a=0 charts miss the node locus. Domination: F is the normalization's fibre-generic valuations over non-fibre-generic points; closed centres follow by specializing to a closed point of the closure plus upper semicontinuity; a normal C' then dominates by ZMT; the unique-lift and closed-or-generic clauses and the finite-near-fibre-generic-points clause all hold. Extraction matches Temkin's (u,pi)/(t-a,pi) blow-up charts. Small cases checked: height 0, empty F, empty curve, a=0 chart, closed centre over a non-closed point of T. There are no duplicates among the rg candidates, no restated clause, no cycle, and uses equal proof_deps. I accept the tool_use proper-fp-permanence, a mathlib-status generic tool. No SGA.
